answer: A sealed-bid issuance auction opens 100 slots per epoch on the trellis board. Each applicant posts a sealed bid, a 5-credit posting fee, and a pigment-marked funding proof, so bids sharing one funding source are grouped and capped at two slots. Winners lock the clearing bid as stake and bridge it into the registry. Clearing starts at 40 credits and rises 10 per 100 bids, so the 1,000th fake pays 130, and 1,000 fakes lock 85,000 credits plus 5,000 in fees. A shill ring fails: grouped proofs expose its shared wallet and forfeit its bonds. One honest applicant pays one clearing bid plus one fee.
